answer: Gross margin is not a useful or standard metric for a company like American Express (AXP). As a financial services and payment network company rather than a manufacturer or retailer, American Express does not produce physical goods or report "cost of goods sold" on its Consolidated Statements of Income. Instead, AXP earns revenues from discount revenue ($30,739 million), net card fees ($6,070 million), service fees ($4,521 million), processed revenue ($1,637 million), and net interest income ($9,895 million) for the year ended December 31, 2022.
rationale: Directly addresses why gross margin is not useful and provides actual FY2022 financial figures for AXP's revenue components.
